fact: A draft of the Data Protection (Data Processors Engagement) Regulations, 2025, dated 6 October 2025 and marked subject to change, would require a processor's agreement to bar transfer of personal data from Malawi to another country except on the controller's written instructions and in compliance with Part VII of the Data Protection Act.

ITLawCo states the Data Protection Act came into force on 3 June 2024 and that sections 38-40 restrict transfers of personal data outside Malawi unless the receiving country has adequate data protection laws or mechanisms such as binding corporate rules are in place.

The Data Protection Act, 2024 (Act No. 3 of 2024), assented 31 January 2024, bars a controller or processor from transferring personal data from Malawi unless the recipient is under a law, binding corporate rule, contractual clause, code of conduct or certification affording adequate protection, or consent or a contract condition applies (s.38, s.39); the Act comes into operation on a date the Minister appoints by Gazette notice (s.1) and the document states no such date, so in-force status is not shown.

The Authority published a compliance guideline and checklist covering the Act's duties, data subject rights, breach notice and cross-border transfers, and a registration requirement for controllers of significant importance; no decision or sanction is reported.
